gloss: to feel proud; to be able to hold one's head high

definitions.gloss: to feel proud; to feel one can hold one's head high among others
definitions.explanation: To feel free of embarrassment in front of other people, usually because of an achievement — often someone else's, such as a family member's. Literally 'one's shoulders are wide.' Far less common than its opposite, {肩身|かたみ}が{狭|せま}い.

examples.japanese: ⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おかげ→おかげ：01362_okage⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}い。
examples.english: Thanks to my son I can hold my head high.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地元|じもと}→地元：09941_jimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{優勝|ゆうしょう}して→優勝する：25496_yuushousuru⟧、⟦ファン→ファン：10065_fan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}い。
examples.english: The local team won the championship, so the fans are walking tall.

examples.japanese: ⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{志望校|しぼうこう}→志望校：18904_shiboukou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合格|ごうかく}して→合格する：27949_goukakusuru⟧、⟦{親戚|しんせき}→親戚：03260_shinseki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}く⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: My daughter got into the school she wanted, so now I can hold my head high even in front of the relatives.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦{赤字|あかじ}→赤字：04712_akaji⟧だった⟦{部署|ぶしょ}→部署：08187_busho⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ようやく⟦{黒字|くろじ}→黒字：04715_kuroji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧、⟦{社内|しゃない}→社内：13731_shanai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}く⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The department had run at a loss for years and finally turned a profit, so we can hold our heads up in the company now.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {肩身|かたみ} (the shoulders; one's standing in others' eyes) + ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ + ⟦{広|ひろ}い→広い：00704_hiroi⟧ (wide).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to come to feel proud
- 〜⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おかげ→おかげ：01362_okage⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}い: to be able to hold one's head high thanks to ~

USAGE:
The pride is social — how one appears to relatives, neighbors, or colleagues — not private satisfaction, which would be ⟦{誇|ほこ}らしい→誇らしい：14181_hokorashii⟧. The negative counterpart ⟦{肩身|かたみ}が{狭|せま}い→肩身が狭い：06891_katamigasemai⟧ (to feel small, ashamed) is much more frequent in everyday speech, and {肩身|かたみ}が{広|ひろ}い is often used precisely as its reversal.
